src: brief v2 §13a (bowling alley: fully playable lanes, the ball-return tunnel as a real squirrel route); brief addendum D4, D5 (eighteen lanes, the larger games room, the shops, the backstage behind the lanes); BUILD_PLAN §3.16-§3.17, W3c #15. Placement: the east commercial grass south of Bowl Lane (studs: the building x 1273.2..1449.8, z -351.2..-501.6; with the forecourt ramp, the rear alley, its end ramps and its fence x 1258..1452, z -338..-522). The origin, floor and yaw are the six-lane house's: lanes 1 to 6 did not move. The site slopes down to the east and to the rear: the front-west corner is cut up to 0.5 st into the ground (a terrain carve box) and the east wing stands on a plinth up to 7 st tall; the alley paving (floorY - 3.5) is above the highest ground behind the lanes. Units: STUDS (not HTML units). Route points are in the alley's local frame [X across the lanes, Y above the floor, D down the lane from the foul line]; tools/compile turns them into world points with Shared/Attractions/AlleyLayout.toWorld. The footprint is everything the alley bakes (the expansion planner keeps every venue site, street and pad out of it).

routes.name: bowling alley ball return (lanes 1-2)
routes.note: The ball return as one enclosed run (Shared/Routes/Enclosure): in at the bent grille in the alley wall (a ground mouth: walk in heading into it), down a short ramp into the duct, under the back of house, the pit and the whole lane at full height (the trough runs deep enough under the pits), up the riser through the hole in the approach floor into the hood, and out with the head in the hood's mouth over the rack (a ledge mouth: Space or a click jumps out toward the bowler, Q drops onto the rack, S goes back in); a crawl inside the hood. Running back out of the grille steps onto the alley on its feet. The ball rolls home along the same curve (Server/Attractions/AttractionService).
